schema_note: schema 2 adds the cells: the column vocabulary, the per-column check against the printed totals, and per record `cells` (committed) beside `cells_first_pass` (read, unreconciled). Schema 1 records carry names only.
division: S. W. Sherman (as written into the printed heading)
read_pass: names and cells (T-0527, piece 5 of 7 of T-0495)
line_count_note: 21 entries, and THE COVERAGE INVENTORY SAID 22. Counted twice on a grid overlay drawn line by line down the names column, the sheet carries 21 names -- John L Hogane at the top to Thomas Downing at the bottom -- and NOTHING below the twenty-first. The form's body runs from the rule at y=561 to the closing rule at y=2970, which is 2409 px, room for about 31 writing lines at this sheet's pitch; the enumerator used the first 21 of them and left the rest of the leaf blank down to the footing row, which he then footed. So this is a SHORT PAGE, not a truncated one: the blank remainder is the enumerator's, not the scan's. The line grid is x-independent line 1 at y=671 with pitch 76.85, taken from the first and last name ink and checked against every name between; it puts line 21 at y=2208, 762 px above the closing rule.

margin_annotation.position: written vertically up the LEFT margin of the leaf, outside the NAMES column, at x~150-290, spanning y~1450-2600 -- beside body lines about 11 to 25. Read by rotating the crop 90 degrees.
margin_annotation.confidence: high for `Chicago` and `Precinct`; the word between them is struck through with four or five heavy horizontal strokes and is NOT recoverable at this resolution -- about four to five letters long. It is recorded as a deletion, not guessed at.
margin_annotation.why_it_matters: as on 33S7-9YYN-3CDH, this is the only thing on the exposure that names the place; the printed heading names only the enumerator's division. The two sheets carry the same annotation in the same hand, and this one shows the enumerator correcting himself mid-phrase -- he wrote a word after `Chicago`, struck it out, and wrote `Precinct`. T-0527 asked for these annotations to be recorded as a finding in their own right.

header_note: the printed heading reads `(No. 4.) SCHEDULE of the whole number of persons within the division allotted to ____` with `S. W. Sherman` written into the blank, and the printed page number `241` at the top right.
form_note: The left (names) sheet of the 1840 population schedule. Columns as printed, left to right: NAMES OF HEADS OF FAMILIES; thirteen FREE WHITE PERSONS - MALES age bands; thirteen FREE WHITE PERSONS - FEMALES age bands; six FREE COLORED PERSONS - MALES bands; six FREE COLORED PERSONS - FEMALES bands.
grid_note: HOW THE CELLS WERE LOCATED. Vertical rules were detected as thin-line maxima of a high-passed darkness profile taken over y=2400..2900, the band of the leaf that carries no writing at all and so returns rules unmixed with ink. Thirty-six of them were assigned their column index and fitted by least squares at rms 2.88 px. THE FIT'S ORIGIN WAS THEN CORRECTED BY +38 px: laid over the written band the first fit stood visibly half a cell left of the printed rules, because the leaf is skewed and the empty band is 700 px below the writing. Boundaries are taken as x = 663 + 80.77 n for n = 0..38, which the printed column heads and the FREE COLORED divider both confirm. THE SAME SKEW SHIFTS THE LINES: a mark in the female columns stands about 26 px lower on the exposure than a mark on the same writing line in the male columns, 1000 px to its left, and the female block was therefore read against a line grid offset by that amount. Both offsets are measured, not assumed, and both are recorded here because a reader re-deriving these cells will hit them.
cells_note: ALL THIRTY-EIGHT COLUMNS CLOSE EXACTLY against the enumerator's own footing row. Nineteen carry a footed figure -- males 6, 8, 4, 3, 13, 10, 5, 2, 3 and females 9, 6, 2, 6, 8, 5, 3, 4, 2, 1 -- and the other nineteen are blank in the footing and blank down the page. 100 persons on 21 lines: 54 male and 46 female. No mark on this sheet needed a judgement call, and none was refused.
free_colored_note: The twenty-four FREE COLORED PERSONS cells are blank on every one of the 21 lines and blank in the footing row, read as a block at magnification against the column grid. A swept-and-empty block is evidence, so the zero is committed rather than left absent.
name_note: The cleanest of this piece's three sheets, and the confidence distribution shows it. Where more than one surname fits, every candidate is named in the record's own note; `as_read` carries `[?]` at a letter POSITION that cannot be resolved (T-0397). Superscript abbreviations are transcribed as written (`Saml`, `Robt`, `Geo`, `Wm`) and expanded only in `normalized`. Lines 3 and 4 carry the same surname on consecutive lines; that is recorded as a neighbour relation and not as a family link.
ipums_note: No IPUMS serial is attached on this sheet; T-0504 does that across all three groups by the age-band fingerprint.

one or two initials, then a surname whose second letter is a tall loop this hand uses for both h and l: Shattuck, Sattuck and Sattick all fit. An earlier pass at low magnification read this as White; at 3.5x it is not White.
one initial; Townsend is legible and matches line 4's surname exactly.
forename written out; the same surname as line 3, on the next line. Consecutive lines are a neighbour relation in enumeration order and are NOT recorded here as a household or family link.
forename Sam closed by a superscript l; Anderson is legible.
both names written out and largely legible; the surname's medial letters are crowded but the terminal -worth is clear.
forename Isaac and a middle initial B. The surname opens on a Ph ligature and closes -elps or -elple: Phelps and Whelple both fit.
the forename runs off the left of the written area into the margin rule and does not resolve. The surname reads Sanford, with Lanford a live alternative on its capital.
forename Abner; Ellison is legible.
forename Washington is written out and clear. The surname's terminal letters run into a flourish: Merritt and Merrill both fit.
forename Geo. The surname is long and reads Breckenridge; Breckinridge fits its medial vowel about as well.
forename Rob closed by a superscript t; Robinson is legible.

forename Joseph. The surname opens on a large looped capital C and its medial letters are crowded and unresolved: Conkie, Comstock, Cortis and Crookee all fit some part of the ink and none fits all of it.
forename and surname both legible; the trailing group reads Jr, the only generational suffix on any of this piece's three sheets.
forename Edward. The surname's medial letters are a run of minims: Cammick, Cormick and Cammitt all fit.
forename John and a middle initial B. The surname opens on a capital C and closes -er, with its medial letters unresolved: Culver, Calver and Cabee all fit.
both names written out and fully legible - the clearest name on the sheet.
forename Sam closed by a superscript l, middle initial E, and Ferris; Fervis fits the medial letters about as well.
forename James. The surname's capital is a large looped form this hand uses for both W and M: Weldin and Meldin both fit.
forename W closed by a superscript m. The surname is short with an unresolved medial vowel: Brier, Brear and Breer all fit.
the last entry on the sheet. Forename Thomas; the surname reads Downing, with Deming a live alternative on its medial letters.
